title: How a Pressure Cooker Works in 60 Seconds 🍲💨 #shorts
description:
A pressure cooker traps steam inside a sealed pot. The extra pressure raises water's boiling point to about 121°C, so food cooks much faster, while a weighted valve lets out extra steam to keep it safe. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#pressurecooker #cooking #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Inside a pressure cooker, water doesn't boil at 100 degrees. It gets to about *121°C*.

steps.label: Seal
steps.text: A rubber *gasket* seals the lid tight, so the steam has *nowhere to go*.

steps.label: Pressure
steps.text: As the water heats, trapped *steam* builds up about *one extra atmosphere* of pressure.

steps.label: Boiling point
steps.text: Higher pressure raises the *boiling point*, so the water gets much *hotter* than normal.

steps.label: Fast cooking
steps.text: That hotter water and steam push heat into the food *faster*, cutting cooking time by up to *70%*.

steps.label: Valve
steps.text: A *weighted valve* lifts and hisses out extra steam, keeping the pressure *steady and safe*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Seal, pressure, *heat*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
